Nebraska property tax is assessed and collected at the local level, and owners can appeal an assessment.

What the official sources say

  • Real property valuation protests must be signed and filed with the county board of equalization after the assessor completes the assessment roll and on or before June 30. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-1502; source)
  • The county board of equalization meets to decide protests beginning on or after June 1 and ending on or before July 25; counties over 100,000 population may extend the hearing deadline to August 10. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-1502; source)
  • A county board of equalization action may be appealed to the Tax Equalization and Review Commission (TERC) on or before August 24, or September 10 if the county extended its protest hearing deadline. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-1510; source)
  • To perfect a TERC appeal, the notice of appeal must be filed within 30 days of the board of equalization's final order. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-1510; source)
  • Protests of omitted-property assessments or clerical-error corrections are filed with the county board within 30 days after mailing of the notice; the board's action may be appealed to TERC within 30 days of its final decision. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-1507; source)
  • Real property is valued at its actual value; agricultural and horticultural land is valued at 75% of actual value. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-201; source)
  • Real estate with taxes unpaid by the first Monday of March after becoming delinquent is subject to sale on or after that date. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-1801; source)
  • The owner, occupant or lienholder may redeem a property sold for taxes; the right expires when the purchaser files an application for tax deed with the county treasurer. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-1824; source)

Nebraska offers property tax relief for qualifying homeowners, and official sources explain the rules.

What the official sources say

  • An owner wanting a homestead exemption must file an application with the county assessor of the county where the homestead is located after February 1 and on or before June 30 of each year. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-3512; source)
  • Failure to file the application timely is a waiver of the exemption for that year. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-3512; source)
  • Where applicable, qualified claimants' homesteads are exempt for a percentage of the exempt amount limited by section 77-3506.03, with the percentage determined by household income. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-3507; source)

This guide covers what official sources say about Nebraska estate and inheritance tax.

What the official sources say

  • Nebraska imposes an inheritance tax (not an estate tax) on interests transferred at death, including jointly held property except the part contributed by the other owner. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-2002; source)
  • Close relatives: 1% of the clear market value received in excess of $100,000 for decedents dying on or after January 1, 2023. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-2004; source)
  • Uncles, aunts, nieces, nephews and their lineal descendants: 11% over $40,000 for decedents dying on or after January 1, 2023. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-2005; source)
  • All other persons: 15% over $25,000 for decedents dying on or after January 1, 2023. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-2006; source)
  • Bequests in trust to an in-state association for exclusively charitable purposes in this state are exempt from inheritance tax. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-2007; source)

A Nebraska deed is recorded with the county office named in the sources below.

What the official sources say

  • After-acquired interest of a grantor does not inure to the grantee if the deed was a quitclaim or special warranty deed. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 76-209; source)
  • Deeds between spouses, ex-spouses (property acquired during marriage) and parent-child without consideration are exempt from documentary stamp tax. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 76-902; source)
  • Register of deeds recording fee for a deed or other instrument is $10 for the first page and $6 for each additional page. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 33-109; source)
  • Recorded instruments need a blank 3 x 8.5 inch space at the top of the first page, size 8.5x11 to 8.5x14, and each party's name typed or printed beneath the signature. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 23-1503.01; source)
  • The statute contemplates instruments submitted electronically (black ink on white background). (Neb. Rev. Stat. 23-1503.01; source)

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

This guide covers what official sources say about Nebraska transfer on death deeds.

What the official sources say

  • A TOD deed must be recorded within 30 days after execution, before the transferor's death, with the register of deeds of the county where the property is located. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 76-3410; source)
  • Thirty days after death, a successor may collect personal property by affidavit if the estate's personal property, less liens, does not exceed $100,000. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 30-24,125; source)
  • Thirty days after death, a successor may file an affidavit with the register of deeds claiming the decedent's real property if the decedent's real property interest does not exceed $100,000 (valued from the assessment rolls less taxes due). (Neb. Rev. Stat. 30-24,129; source)
  • A personal representative has the same power over title to estate property as an absolute owner, exercisable without notice, hearing or court order unless the court orders otherwise. (Neb. Rev. Stat. 30-2472; source)
